hypotheses.title: Classification threshold sensitivity
hypotheses.explanation: Late or missed warnings in logistic_regression arise because its thresholding is less sensitive or less sharply tuned to gradual sensor dropouts or stuck states, unlike xgboost_augmented which better maintains detection margins.
hypotheses.alternative: The logistic_regression model's limited feature complexity causes weak fault pattern representation, reducing early detection capability despite threshold settings.

hypotheses.title: Feature representation differences
hypotheses.explanation: The xgboost_augmented model leverages augmented input features that distinctly separate fault signatures from normal operation, allowing near-perfect detection and minimal late/missed warnings, whereas logistic_regression lacks these enriched features leading to detection gaps.
hypotheses.alternative: Differences in model family and training approach, not feature augmentation alone, cause the observed detection performance gap between models.

gaps: Lack of preprocessing and feature contribution records prevents assessing whether missingness handling or feature scaling differ meaningfully between models.
Absence of equipment fold outcome data restricts understanding of how these shortfalls generalize across data partitions.

next_tests.title: Threshold adjustment impact on dropout event detection
next_tests.procedure: Replay scoring traces for logistic_regression with progressively lower detection thresholds on dropout fault patterns to assess sensitivity and detection timing shifts.
next_tests.expected_signal: Lower thresholds yield increased timely detection and reduced missed or late warnings on dropout faults for logistic_regression.
next_tests.if_signal_observed: Confirms threshold tuning is a key factor limiting detection; improved thresholds could close sensitivity gap relative to xgboost_augmented.
next_tests.if_signal_absent: Suggests logistic_regression's underlying model complexity or representation, not threshold choice, primarily limits detection performance.

next_tests.title: Feature importance comparison via surrogate analysis
next_tests.procedure: Analyze available paired histories to compare feature utility or importance proxies in both models, focusing on fault patterns with late or missed warnings for logistic_regression.
next_tests.expected_signal: Xgboost_augmented shows stronger usage or clearer discriminative features related to dropout and stuck fault patterns compared to logistic_regression.
next_tests.if_signal_observed: Supports that augmented feature representation drives improved detection and robustness.
next_tests.if_signal_absent: Indicates model architecture or training differences could dominate, minimizing augmentation benefit in isolation.
